core_obligations: Identify the two zeroth cohomologies: the kernel of the localization map computes the cohomology with support in the closed subscheme, from which the equality with the ideal-torsion submodule and its torsionness follow (proof lines 2125-2134)
Higher vanishing for the torsion: the torsion submodule is its own local cohomology in both versions, which gives the vanishing of all its higher cohomology (proof lines 2135-2137)

The quotient: it has no torsion by the cited statement, so its zeroth cohomology vanishes in both versions, and the long exact cohomology sequence transfers the higher cohomology of the original module to the quotient (proof lines 2138-2142)
proof_roadmap: H^0_I(M) = M[I^∞] 是 I-幂挠；由 local-cohomology-adjoint 引理，H^0_Z(M) = Ker(M → ∏ M_{f_i}) ⇒ 两者相等，且 N = 该值。
N 自身 I-幂挠 ⇒ 由 adjoint 引理 RΓ_I(N) = N 与 RΓ_Z(N) = N ⇒ 高次上同调为零。
由 More on Algebra 的 divide-by-torsion，M' = M/N 无 I-幂挠 ⇒ H^0_I(M') = H^0_Z(M') = 0；再由长正合列得 M 与 M' 的高次上同调相等。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement identifies the zeroth local cohomology of a module with support in a finitely generated ideal with the closed subscheme version, and shows that after dividing by the common torsion submodule the local cohomology concentrates in degree zero while the higher cohomology is unchanged (author lemma at source lines 2111-2123, label lemma-divide-by-torsion). The proof (source lines 2125-2143) computes the zeroth cohomology as a kernel of localizations, reads off torsionness and the vanishing of the higher cohomology of the torsion submodule from the adjoint description, and uses the torsion freeness of the quotient together with the long exact cohomology sequence (proof lines 2138-2142). The comparison of the two zeroth cohomologies is the substance. H3.
